reason: Both conversations skipped the sensible levelling and noise-localisation checks and leaned on 'almost certainly' language, but Conversation 2 kept the plausible causes broader (support rollers vs idler pulley), discovered the customer's back injury, and escalated sensibly to an engineer, which matches the expected outcome for someone who cannot tilt or move the unit. Conversation 1 never learned about the mobility constraint, narrowed prematurely to pulley/belt while ignoring rollers, and told the customer to order a pulley-and-belt kit without any panel inspection confirming the worn part, which is an unsupported part recommendation. Conversation 2 was also honest about being unable to verify part availability, though it was slightly over-cautious in calling the job not owner-safe.
